items.summary: If someone leaves the faucet running in your bathroom and the house floods, it's easy to assign responsibility for the damage. But for other disasters—bigger, more complicated and costlier ones—the link between cause and effect isn't as clear.

items.title: Kibble with microbial proteins appeals to cats and dogs in new study
items.summary: In a new study, cats and dogs showed a short-term preference for kibble containing some protein derived from microorganisms over kibble containing only standard animal-derived protein. items.title: A horse named Pea is first to test focused ultrasound treatment of skin tumors called sarcoids
items.summary: There is no "one-fix-for-all" solution for sarcoids, said Sophie Bogers, an assistant professor of large animal surgery. Many require chemotherapy or invasive surgery. But she wants a better solution.

items.title: Hormone-disrupting chemicals found in range of natural and drinking water sources
items.summary: A new study has found that chemicals that can affect fertility and reproductive health are contaminating natural and drinking water supplies. items.title: Exercise keeps astronauts' hearts strong enough for flight to Mars
items.summary: Intense exercise during long spaceflights helps maintain heart structure and function within a range needed to tolerate the low-gravity environment of Mars, a study co-led by a UT Southwestern Medical Center researcher suggests. items.title: Variations in virus tails may help predict which phages kill more bacterial strains
items.summary: Bacteriophages—or phages, for short—are viruses that kill bacteria, and scientists have been studying them for decades as a possible solution to antibiotic-resistant infections. items.title: Facial recognition trial by police in Australia delivered strong results. But was it an ethical success?
items.summary: The results of Australia's first live facial recognition trial have been released. Since June 2026, the Western Australian Police Force has been testing the technology across metropolitan and regional WA.

items.title: Arctic Sea Ice Reaches 2026 Annual Minimum Extent
items.summary: Arctic sea ice reached its annual minimum extent on Sept. 12, according to NASA and the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) at the University of Colorado Boulder. items.summary: A team from SUNY Polytechnic Institute has designed a quantum rule-based simulator known as Quantum Tic-Tac-Toe. items.title: Roaming black holes may tell the hidden history of galaxies
items.summary: If you want to understand the origins of black holes, Yale astronomers say, you need to look beyond the centers of galaxies and start searching in the nooks and crannies. items.title: New mining map highlights damage caused by extracting metals for your smartphone
items.summary: The most sustainable smartphone is the one you currently own. An estimated 80% of your phone's negative impact on the environment happens before the first minute of use—before it is even unboxed.

items.title: Bizarre new dinosaur with giant claws discovered in China
items.summary: It walked on two legs and may have looked like a feathered bear with giant claws. Meet Kayrasaurus changliensis—well, its almost complete skeleton, to be precise.

items.title: Spin waves inside a nano-oscillator imaged for the first time
items.summary: For the first time, researchers have directly imaged the magnetization dynamics inside a spin Hall nano-oscillator—a nanoscale device that converts direct current into tunable microwave signals and is a promising building block for energy-efficient wireless communication and brain-inspired computing

items.summary: Studying exoplanets has given astronomers insights into the characteristics that could help them find life beyond Earth. items.title: How diffractive solar sails could stop a killer asteroid at 100 km/s
items.summary: Asteroids don't come with a warning label that they might one day hit Earth. While we don't know of any currently on course to do so, we are finding thousands of new ones each year, and there's always a chance that one could.

items.title: DIY filter systems improve air quality in classrooms
items.summary: As students return to school and cold and flu season begins, researchers are studying ways to improve indoor air quality and reduce the risk of airborne disease transmission.

items.title: Report calls for government to introduce a charge on disposable cups
items.summary: Around 2.5 billion single-use cups are used in the U.K. every year, yet fewer than 1% are recycled. They contribute to litter, contaminate recycling streams and increase waste management and street cleaning costs for local authorities and taxpayers.
